title: DHCP relay forwards incorrect DHCP client packet to DHCP server(in case of DHCP packet without payload)
author: ppikh
body:
[dump_on_dhcp_server_side.pcap.gz](https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/files/5603026/dump_on_dhcp_server_side.pcap.gz)
[dump_on_dut_dhcp_client_vlan.pcap.gz](https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/files/5603029/dump_on_dut_dhcp_client_vlan.pcap.gz)

**DHCP relay forwards incorrect DHCP client packet to DHCP server(in case of DHCP packet without payload)**

DHCP relay forwards incorrect DHCP client packet to DHCP server(in case of DHCP packet without payload)
Issue happens in case when send DHCP packet via scapy without DHCP payload.
Packet example:  Ether(src="0c:42:a1:17:e6:fd",dst="ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff")/IP(src="0.0.0.0",dst="255.255.255.255")/UDP(sport=68,dport=67)/BOOTP(chaddr='0c42a117e6fd'.decode('hex'),xid=RandInt())/DHCP()

**Setup**:
SONiC device has 2 connected Linux hosts(host A, host B)
Host A connected from port enp4s0f1 to SONiC port Ethernet124
Host B connected from port enp6s0f1 to SONiC port Ethernet60
Host A acts as DCHP client, 
Host B acts as DCHP server and has next network configuration:
sudo ip addr add 69.0.0.2/24 dev enp6s0f1
sudo ip route add 69.0.1.0/24 via 69.0.0.1

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Configure DUT:
sudo config interface ip add Ethernet60 69.0.0.1/24
sudo config vlan add 690
sudo config vlan member add --untagged 690 Ethernet124
sudo config interface ip add Vlan690 69.0.1.1/24
sudo config vlan dhcp_relay add 690 69.0.0.2
2. Send from DHCP client empty DHCP packet using scapy:
pkt = Ether(src="0c:42:a1:17:e6:fd",dst="ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff")/IP(src="0.0.0.0",dst="255.255.255.255")/UDP(sport=68,dport=67)/BOOTP(chaddr='0c42a117e6fd'.decode('hex'),xid=RandInt())/DHCP()
sendp(pkt, iface='enp4s0f1')
3. Check packet to DHCP server side

**Describe the results you received:**
DHCP packet arrived to DHCP server, but it modified and have some unexpected data. For example in packet added option 12 - with some hostname, also added option 50 - with requested IP - which is not in DHCP server subnet and other.
See attached PCAP files(use: "tar -xf file_name.pcap..gz"  for unpack).

**Describe the results you expected:**
DHCP packet forwarded to DHCP server without modification, only DHCP relay option 82 should be added.


**Additional information you deem important (e.g. issue happens only occasionally):**
Issue reproduce only in case of DHCP packet without payload.

comments.author: tahmed-dev
comments.body: @ppikh Thanks for reporting. This is an interesting scenario. Can you please instead of capturing from client/servers ends, do packet capture from the relay vlan port it is listening to and from uplink ports it sends packet through?

comments.author: ppikh
comments.body:
@tahmed-dev file **dump_on_dut_dhcp_client_vlan.pcap.gz** created on DUT(SONiC) side on VLAN interface 690.
I used: tcpdump -i Vlan690 -w file.pcap

File **dump_on_dhcp_server_side.pcap.gz** created on DHCP server side

Do you still need packet on interface to which connected DHCP server from DUT side, like run: "tcpdump -i Ethernet60 -w file.pcap"?

comments.author: tahmed-dev
comments.body: @ppikh Yes, please. I want to make sure that any option addition is indeed coming from the relay. The options are client based options and the relay doesn't how to fill them in. So, it is either sending garbage data, or it was indeed received that way. To rule out the latter, it is good to see what is being received on the downlink of the vlan interface. Also, capture on the uplink interface + default route interface will show outgoing packet from the relay.

comments.author: osydoren
comments.body:
@ppikh
Hi. I started working with this issue and I tried to reproduce it on my setup. I have Mellanox Spectrum SN2700 switch and I used the build from master branch. But I am having problems. I applied the configuration you described in the issue, the configuration is being applied successfully. Next, on the client DUT using Scapy, I generated DHCP discovery packet and sent it in the direction of the switch, destination mac address is broadcast, the source IP is set to all zero, the destination IP is set to all 255 since we send this packet in the direction of the Relay Agent and the Relay Agent should modify this packet into unicast and send it to the DHCP server. But in my case, all the packets that came to the switch are dropped in Vlan690. I see that packets enter the physical port, the corresponding counter in the statistics is incremented, also I see that RX_ERR counter from the rifcounters for Vlan690 being incremented, so all the packets are dropped in my case and I was not been able to find exact reason why packets are dropped. I sorted out around this and I can say that I see 3 possible reasons why my packages are dropped, 1) broadcast mac address - perhaps the flooding control is enabled by default and did not find cli commands to check it, 2) 0.0.0.0 source IP - it seems to me that this is invalid value and I saw a test in Sonic repository for this, the test specifically checks that packets that contain such a value in the IP header should be dropped, 3) 255.255.255.255 destination IP - I think the same as in 2 but may be wrong. If I change all these fields to make packet unicast with valid IPs it stops dropping it.

Based on this, I want to ask you, did you attach the full configuration to the issue, or is there something else that needs to be configured so that these packets are not dropped by the switch, perhaps something needs to be configured additionally.
Since I do not have much experience in relay agent and how it works in sonic, I want to ask you what needs to be configured additionally, or perhaps you have any assumptions based on the information I provided that something is not working correctly on my config or is invalid or maybe I am doing something wrong or I should look at something else.
Any help from you would be greatly appreciated.
Thanks

Packages do not reach the DHCP server from the client.

linkedPullRequests.title: [relay]: Prevent Buffer Overrun Of Malformed DHCP Packet
linkedPullRequests.author: tahmed-dev
linkedPullRequests.body:
The add/strip relay agent options do not take into account the buffer
length and so it is possible to overrun the buffer. The issue will
result in contents from previous packet being added to the current one.

closes #6052  
resolves #6052 

signed-off-by: Tamer Ahmed <tamer.ahmed@microsoft.com>
